source_quality.text_layer: usable prose; formula glyphs are lost and the file is not valid UTF-8, so every numbered equation was read from the page rasters

task_reconstruction: Set the best levels for the Great Lakes and hold them with the dams, using a network whose flow follows the upstream level, a six-group satisfaction score, and a look-ahead release solved by a genetic search.

section_map.summary: summary: the two models, the control rule, the six groups and the limits
introduction: the stakes, the five tasks and the work-flow figure
six assumptions, each with its justification
the lakes numbered and the notation table
the network, the level balance and the rejected difference hypothesis
the upstream-level law, the weak pair and the fitted lines
rain, evaporation and the ice jam factor
the six stakeholder groups and the influence-interest matrix
the weights, the optimal level and the predictive-control cost
the inherited release rule and its 2017 weakness
the modified rule curve and the start of the 2017 test
the simulation charts and the stakeholder impacts
the environmental sensitivity, then the strengths and weaknesses

contributions.summary: a network of the lakes with the flow on each river fitted as a line in the upstream level
six stakeholder satisfaction functions weighted into one level that maximises the total
a look-ahead release, solved by a genetic search, offered as a sharpening of the standing rule

dependency_graph.carries: the fitted river flows and the level balance the release acts on
the level that maximises stakeholder satisfaction, used as the ideal

assumptions.summary: the lakes are treated as a network, to shrink the tangle
two neighbouring lakes are merged into one node, no river separating them
rain and evaporation are kept and the rest set aside, on one cited study

data_and_preprocessing.summary: table 2: mean level and spread per lake, the lowest lake read from the raster
table 3: the fitted line for every reach
table 5: the six weights, which sum to 0.90

models.summary: the network: the level balance, the linear flow law, rain, evaporation and ice
the satisfaction model: six scores, the weights and the level that maximises the sum
the controller: the predictive-control cost, the genetic search and the modified release

verification.summary: the 2017 simulation is read against the ideal levels by eye
three correlation coefficients back the upstream-level law
rain, snowmelt and ice are each given a qualitative verdict

results_trace.summary: the flow follows the upstream level, one river excepted and explained by the dams
apart from a few days the simulated year sits close to the ideal levels
the periods of drift are laid over the satisfaction scores

writing_logic.summary: the summary names both models, concedes the limits and points forward
a wrong guess is tested, replaced and then dropped before the kept one
the inherited rule is praised before its flaw is named

language_observations.summary: a formula is handed over with a fixed turn: can be represented by the following formula, the formula is as follows
a result is set against the expectation: the analysis revealed a low correlation, which contradicts the expected phenomena
praise is given and then withdrawn: the algorithm demonstrates several strengths, however the performance highlighted a critical weakness
the close is a belief, not a proof: we believe that our approach can become a more effective tool

visualization_observations.summary: figure 5: the river running downhill from the higher lake
figure 7: the heatmap of upstream level against outflow
figure 9: the evaporation calculation as a chain of boxes
figure 10: the simulated 2017 levels against the ideal

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: a judge looking for a usable plan gets a network, a named satisfaction score and a release rule tied to the plan already in force
the paper reviews the standing rule before changing it, which is what a judge would expect of advice to the body that runs it

weaknesses.summary: the dock score repeats the shipping function, keeps its label, and leaves the level above the band undefined
the hydropower score drops to zero at a low level while the prose describes a plateau
the modified release rule is printed identical to the rule it claims to change
the cost sums over four lakes, the bounds allow five and the control acts at two
the fitted table uses a fifth lake the notation never defines
the prose swaps the two densities in the evaporation formula
the vapour pressure is said to use humidity, and the formula has no humidity term
the precipitation balance marks an outflow with an undefined sign
four flow limits are named and never written

independent_extensions.summary: the standing release rule kept and offered with one added deviation term
